I've ported the program to Kotlin. The source is `src/WordFreq.kt` and uses only the standard library. `build.sh` compiles it to `build/wordfreq.jar` and writes `./app`, a small launcher script that runs `java` on that jar.

`node check.mjs` builds from a clean directory and passes all 6 example cases. I also compared it with the Python original on a generated 50 MB word file and a 20 MB file of random bytes. The output was identical both times, and the 50 MB run took about 0.3 s.

DONE
